name: Tarot of the Abbé de Marolles 1637
description: Three-player trick-taking Tarot recorded by the Abbé de Marolles in 1637 at Nevers. Played with a 66-card pack (Italian-suited Tarot with lowest three of each suit removed). Players score for declaring card combinations, for winning or losing Tarots (Kings, Fool, Trump I, XXI), for card points in tricks, and for Ultimo (last trick with King or Trump I).

history.origins: Michel de Marolles, Abbot of Villeloin, recorded in 1637 that he played Tarot at Nevers with Princess Louise-Marie de Gonzague-Nevers (later Queen of Poland). She had added innovations and asked him to have the rules printed; these are the oldest known printed Tarot rules.
timeline: 1637: Rules printed in Nevers (Regles dv iev des tarots).
18th century: Similar three-player Tarot spread in Europe.
history.cultural: Played in French aristocratic circles; Nevers lay between Paris and Lyon.
history.evolution: Princess Marie-Louise's version used a 66-card pack and had all three players discard before play; the 78-card variant (25 each to opponents, 28 to dealer, dealer discards 3) may be the earlier form.

setup.players: Three players, each playing for themselves; no partnerships.
setup.deck: 66-card pack: Italian-suited Tarot (78 cards) with the lowest three cards of each suit removed. 22 triomphes (21 trumps I–XXI plus the Fool); 4 suits with 4 court cards (King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack) and 7 numerals each.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles; player to dealer's left cuts (cut card shown; if it is a Tarot, dealer receives one marque from each opponent). Dealer deals 4 rounds of 5 cards to each player, then one more card to each other player and 4 to himself: non-dealers receive 21 cards each, dealer 24. The two non-dealers each discard one card and the dealer discards four; no trumps or Tarots may be discarded (penalty: two marques to each opponent). Discards count in the discarder's favour at end of play.

rules.objective: Score marques by declaring combinations, winning Tarots in tricks, avoiding capture of Tarots, making Ultimo (last trick with King or Trump I), and having above-average card points in tricks; losers pay the winner(s).
rules.gameplay: After the deal and discards, players in turn declare combinations (Tarots, Kings and Fool, Triomphes, Imperials, Brizigole, Tous les trois) and receive marques from opponents. Player to dealer's right leads; suit must be followed; if unable to follow, must play a trump (no need to overtake). Highest trump wins, or highest card of led suit. Fool may be played as excuse (s'excuser) in any trick except the last; it is shown and discarded to holder's tricks and cannot be captured. At end of play, card points in tricks (plus discards) are counted; players below average pay the winner(s).
keyRules: Follow suit; if unable, play a trump. No obligation to overtake when playing trump.
Fool (Math) may be played as excuse except in the last trick; holder must excuse before last trick or pay two marques to each opponent.
Tarots (Kings, Fool, Trump I, XXI): winning one in a trick pays one marque from each opponent; losing one to an opponent pays one marque to each.
Ultimo: win last trick with King or Trump I (Bagat) for 6 marques from each opponent; if King or Trump I played to last trick but does not win, pay 6 marques to each opponent.
Card points: Tarots 5 each, Queens 4, Cavaliers 3, Jacks 2; total pack 74. Below 25 points = loser, 25+ = winner.

strategy.basic: Protect Tarots; try to excuse the Fool before the last trick. Declare combinations you hold to collect marques.
strategy.intermediate: Count trumps and high cards; time when to play Tarots to avoid capture. Save a high trump for Ultimo when you have King or Trump I.
strategy.advanced: Maximise declarations (Tarots, Kings+Fool, Triomphes, Imperials, Brizigole, Tous les trois) before play; manage card points so you finish above 25; avoid losing Tarots in tricks.
tips: Illegal discard (trump or Tarot) costs two marques to each opponent.
Ultimo (last trick with King or Trump I) is worth 6 marques from each opponent and is the most important scoring element.

variations.name: 78-card game
variations.description: Without the Princess's innovations: full 78-card pack; 25 cards each to dealer's opponents, 28 to dealer who discards 3; no discard by non-dealers. Similar to classic 3-player Tarot in 18th-century Europe.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Override details not specified in source; add when variant rules are expanded.

scoring.description: Marques are won or paid for: declarations (Tarots, Kings+Fool, Triomphes, Imperials, Brizigole, Tous les trois), playing or capturing Tarots in tricks, Ultimo (last trick with King or Trump I), and card points (Tarots 5, Queens 4, Cavaliers 3, Jacks 2; pack total 74). Below 25 points = loser pays winner(s); above 25 = winner collects.
scoring.winCondition: After the hand, the player(s) with above-average card points (25 or more) win; the player(s) with below average (24 or less) pay. Two losers each pay the single winner per 5-point band below 25; two winners each collect from the single loser per 5-point band above 25. Ultimo (last trick with King or Trump I) pays 6 marques from each opponent.
